sources.fullCitation: “Kleine Bilder vom Semmering-Rennen.” Drawings by Hans Schaukal; the caricature of Franz Wenzler is captioned “Direktor Franz Wenzler.” Die Bühne (Vienna), no. 203 (1928): 20. ANNO – Austrian Newspapers Online, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek. Accessed 26 August 2026.
sources.title: Kleine Bilder vom Semmering-Rennen
sources.creator: Hans Schaukal (draughtsman)
sources.researchNote: The page settles the identification. Its text calls him outright “der Theaterdirektor Franz Wenzler als Rennfahrer. Oder der Rennfahrer Franz Wenzler als Theaterdirektor. Wie man will,” and sets his seasons “in der Rotenturmstraße”, the street off which the Wiener Kammerspiele stand, the house he directed from 1926 and owned from 1931 before returning to Berlin and to the comedies scored by Kaper and Jurmann in 1932. The report describes the meeting as a festival of cars, hotels and Mercedes, names Rudolf Caracciola as the certain winner and Count Tivadar Zichy among the Hungarians on Bugatti, and credits every drawing to Hans Schaukal — on the evidence of the years and the trade, Johann Wolfgang Schaukal, son of the writer Richard von Schaukal, who is recorded as a theatre draughtsman in Vienna and Berlin from 1928 to 1931.

media.title: Franz Wenzler — caricature by Hans Schaukal, Die Bühne, 1928
media.description: Pen caricature of Franz Wenzler in profile, wearing a driving cap and a thick rolled scarf, signed by the draughtsman. It appeared on a page of sketches from the Semmering motor race, captioned simply “Direktor Franz Wenzler.”
media.altText: Pen-and-ink caricature of a man’s head in profile, in a flat driving cap and a thick rolled scarf, with the artist’s signature beneath.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. The drawings on the page are credited to Hans Schaukal, that is Johann Wolfgang Schaukal (1900-1981), who worked as a theatre draughtsman in Vienna and Berlin in exactly those years; on that identification the seventy-year term after the author’s death runs to the end of 2051. The local 874 × 1150 pixel reproduction is used for scholarly identification of a documented Kaper collaborator, with the draughtsman, the holding institution and the unresolved permission stated alongside it.
